Run It End-to-End\n12. Free Tier vs Paid Key\n13. Common Errors & Fixes\n14. What to Build Next\n1. What You're Building\nA new billing clerk joins a Bengaluru distributor. Nobody hands them a manual. They price an invoice, the accountant sends back a correction, and they write the lesson in a notebook. A month later the notebook is the manual.\nYou'll build that clerk as an agent. It prices GST invoices for a made-up company, Kaveri Traders, which has four billing rules nobody writes down. The agent is never told them. After each wrong answer it reads the accountant's correction and adds one bullet to its own playbook, a JSON file on disk.\nOn eight invoices it has never seen, the empty playbook gets 4 of 16 attempts right (only the two easy controls). After one pass over ten training invoices, the agent's three-bullet playbook gets 16 of 16. No fine-tuning, no weights changed. Only the text in front of the model changed.\nThe method is ACE, Agentic Context Engineering (Zhang et al., Stanford, SambaNova and UC Berkeley, ICLR 2026). It splits the work across three roles:\nRole | Job\nGenerator | Does the task, using the playbook, and says which bullets it used\nBuild an Agent That Writes Its Own Playbook - ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) in 45 Minutes 2"

      "index": 4,
      "text": "Role | Job\nReflector | Compares the answer with the ground truth and finds the lesson\nCurator | Turns the lesson into a small delta: a few new bullets, never a rewrite\nThe delta is the idea worth learning. Most \"self-improving prompt\" setups ask an LLM to rewrite the whole prompt after each mistake. ACE treats the playbook like a git repo instead: you add a line, and nothing else moves. In the paper, ACE beat strong baselines by 10.6% on agent tasks and 8.6% on finance tasks.\n2. Architecture Overview\nInvoice → Generator → Checker: exact total? / Accountant correction → Reflector → Curator: ADD bullets / Votes: helpful or harmful → Python merge and prune → Playbook JSON\nThe Generator reads the whole playbook and the invoice, and returns a total plus the IDs of the bullets it relied on. A plain Python checker compares that total with the true one.\nIf the answer is wrong, the Reflector sees the clerk's working and the accountant's line-by-line correction. It names the missed rule and votes on each bullet the clerk used: helpful, harmful or neutral.\nThe Curator reads that lesson and returns only the new bullets to ADD. Then plain Python does the rest. It gives each bullet an ID, skips near-duplicates, bumps the vote counters, and drops any bullet that has misled the clerk more often than it helped.\nThat last part matters most. The purple boxes are LLM calls. The green merge box is ordinary code. No LLM ever writes the playbook file. The official ACE code works the same way, and its Curator can only ADD.\nWhat lives where\nBuild an Agent That Writes Its Own Playbook - ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) in 45 Minutes 3"
    },

      "index": 5,
      "text": "Piece | Built when | Lives in\nInvoices and the ground-truth calculator | Written once, by you | src/tasks.py\nThe playbook | Grows after every wrong answer | playbook.json on disk\nReadable copy of the playbook | Rewritten after every step | handbook.md on disk\nHistory of every change | One line appended per step | delta_log.jsonl on disk\nGenerator, Reflector, Curator | One API call each, per invoice | Groq's servers, nothing kept\nMost demos in this series forget everything when the program exits. This one doesn't. The playbook is a file, so a second run of train starts with everything the first run learned. That is the whole point: the agent gets better across runs, and the model never changes.\nHow each piece works, on one invoice\nTraining invoice T01 is 12 bags of basmati rice at Rs 455 with 5% GST, plus Rs 650 freight. With an empty playbook, the Generator taxes the freight at 5% like the rice and answers Rs 6,383. The truth is Rs 6,500, because Kaveri Traders always taxes freight at 18%.\nThe Reflector reads the correction, which has a line saying \"GST on freight, always @18%\". It returns the insight \"Freight charges attract 18% GST... product GST rates apply only to product line items.\"\nThe Curator turns that into one ADD operation. Python stores it as [rul-00001] Apply 18% GST to all freight (non-product) charges regardless of the product GST rates. On T04, three invoices later, the Generator uses rul-00001, gets the answer right, and the Reflector votes it helpful. Its counter goes to helpful=1.\nIn a real product this loop would run inside your service, after each task where you can get feedback: a failed test, a customer correction, a rejected ticket. The playbook would live in a database row instead of a JSON file.\n3. Prerequisites & Setup\nBuild an Agent That Writes Its Own Playbook - ACE (Agentic Context Engineering) in 45 Minutes 4"

      "text": "5. The Invoices and the Hidden Rules\nThe agent needs work where it will fail at first, for reasons it can't guess. Kaveri Traders has four billing rules:\n1. Freight is always taxed at 18%, whatever rate the goods carry.\n2. The trade discount applies to goods only, never to freight.\n3. GST is rounded to the nearest rupee on every line, then summed.\n4. Customers outside Karnataka pay a flat Rs 200 e-way handling fee, with no GST.\nRules 1 and 4 are made up on purpose. Under real GST law, freight bundled with goods usually takes the goods' rate, so a model's general knowledge points the wrong way.       "text": "The IDs let the Generator say \"I used rul-00001\", and that is what makes per-bullet voting possible. The counters show the model which bullets have a track record. Start src/playbook.py:\n# src/playbook.py\n\"\"\"The playbook: itemized bullets with IDs and helpful/harmful counters.\n\nInputs:  delta operations from the Curator, bullet tags from the Reflector.\nOutputs: an updated Playbook, saved as playbook.json and rendered as handbook.md.\n\nEvery change here is plain Python. No LLM ever rewrites this file. The Curator\ncan only propose new bullets, and the Reflector can only vote on old ones.       "text": "def save(playbook: Playbook, path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Write the playbook to disk as JSON.\"\"\"\n    path.write_text(json.dumps(asdict(playbook), indent=2, ensure_ascii=False), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n\n\ndef render(playbook: Playbook) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The playbook as the Generator reads it, grouped by section.\"\"\"\n    if not playbook.bullets:\n        return \"(empty - no lessons learned yet)\"\n    parts = []\n    for section in SECTIONS:\n        rows = [b for b in playbook.bullets if b.section == section]\n        if rows:\n            parts.append(f\"## {section.upper()}\")\n            parts += [f\"[{b.id}] helpful={b.helpful} harmful={b.harmful} :: {b.content}\" for b in rows]\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts)\nNow the delta merge, the heart of ACE. apply_delta() takes the Curator's ADD operations and appends each one as a new bullet. It touches nothing else. Two guards run first.\nThe first strips any [rul-00002] helpful=0 harmful=0 :: prefix. The model sees that format in the playbook and copies it into new bullets.
